A message (request, response, or notification) with `"jsonrpc": "2.0"` specified as
[required by JSON-RPC 2.0 Specification][1].

[1]: https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#compatibility

Protocol-level notifications, which either side can send.

Their methods start with `$/`. Acting on one is optional, because it might not
be implementable in every Client or Agent. For example, a single-threaded
synchronous implementation can do little to react to a `$/cancel_request`
notification. An Agent or Client MAY ignore a `$/` notification it cannot act on.

Notifications do not expect a response.

anyOf.title: CancelRequestNotification
anyOf.description:
Cancels an ongoing request.

This is a notification sent by the side that sent a request to cancel that request.

Upon receiving this notification, the receiver:

1. MAY cancel the corresponding request activity and all nested activities
2. MAY send any pending notifications.
3. MUST still send a response for the original request. If the request already finished
   or is not cancelled, that is its normal response. If it is cancelled, it is either the
   method's defined cancellation result (for example an inserted `session/prompt`, or a
   `cancelled` permission outcome) or an error with code `-32800` (Request cancelled).

Receivers MUST ignore this notification for an unknown or already-answered request ID,
and MUST NOT send a second response for it.

See protocol docs: [Request Cancellation](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/cancellation)

anyOf.title: RequestPermissionRequest
anyOf.description:
Requests permission from the user for an operation.

Called by the Agent when it needs user authorization before executing
a potentially sensitive operation. The Client presents the options
to the user and returns their decision.

After `session/cancel`, the Agent stops waiting for requests of the cancelled
foreground work and MUST cancel them with `$/cancel_request`. The Client
answers a cancelled request with the `cancelled` outcome.

If the selected option has kind `reject_once` or `reject_always`, the Agent MUST NOT
perform the requested operation.

An error response is not approval, and neither is a connection that ends
before the Client answers. The Agent MUST NOT treat either as approval.

See protocol docs: [Requesting Permission](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/tool-calls#requesting-permission)

ToolCallUpdate.description:
Represents an upsert for a tool call that the language model has requested.

Tool calls are actions that the Agent executes on behalf of the language model,
such as reading files, executing code, or fetching data from external sources.

Only `toolCallId` is required. Other fields have patch semantics:
omitted fields leave the existing tool call value unchanged, `null` clears or
unsets the value, and concrete values replace the previous value. For
collection fields, concrete arrays replace the previous collection, and both
`null` and `[]` clear the collection. A concrete `_meta` object instead
patches the stored metadata by top-level key. When a Client receives a tool
call ID it has not seen before, omitted fields start at their protocol defaults.

See protocol docs: [Tool Calls](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/tool-calls)

toolCallId.description: Unique identifier for this tool call within the session.

name.description:
Programmatic name of the tool being invoked.

This field is optional and has patch semantics. Omission means no
change, `null` clears the name, and a string replaces it. For a tool
call ID the Client has not seen before, omission or `null` means that no
tool name is available.

title.description:
Human-readable plain-text title describing what the tool is doing.

Omission leaves the title unchanged, `null` unsets it, and a string replaces it.
A new tool call starts without a title.

kind.description:
The category of tool being invoked.
Helps Clients choose appropriate icons and UI treatment.

Omission leaves the kind unchanged, `null` resets it to `other`, and a value replaces it.
A new tool call starts as `other`.

status.description:
Current execution status of the tool call.

Omission leaves the status unchanged, `null` resets it to `pending`, and a value
replaces it. A new tool call starts as `pending`. Agents do not move a tool call
back to `pending` once it has another status.

content.description: Content produced by the tool call.

locations.description:
File locations affected by this tool call.
Enables "follow-along" features in Clients.

rawOutput.description: Raw output returned by the tool.

capabilities.description:
Client-initiated controls this tool call currently supports, such as cancellation.

Omission leaves the capabilities unchanged, `null` clears them, and an object replaces
the whole previous value. A new tool call starts with none.

_meta.description:
The _meta property is reserved by ACP to allow Clients and Agents to attach additional
metadata to their interactions. Omitted leaves the stored metadata unchanged. `null`
clears it. An object patches the stored metadata by top-level key: keys it omits are
unchanged, a key set to `null` is removed, and any other value replaces that key's
stored value without merging nested objects. Beyond this patch rule, implementations
MUST NOT assign meaning to keys they do not recognize.

See protocol docs: [Metadata Patches](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/extensibility#metadata-patches)

ContentBlock.description:
Content blocks represent displayable information in the Agent Client Protocol.

Content blocks appear in:
- User prompts sent via `session/prompt`
- Language model output reported through `session/update` notifications as
  message updates or streamed chunks
- Progress updates and results from tool calls

This structure is compatible with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so Agents can
forward content from MCP tool outputs without transformation.

See protocol docs: [Content](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/content)

extensions.

Requires the `image` prompt capability when included in prompts.

Requires the `audio` prompt capability when included in prompts.

SkillReference.description:
**UNSTABLE**

This capability is not part of the spec yet, and may be removed or changed at any point.

A reference to a skill that the user invokes with a prompt.

The Client sends it in `session/prompt` to invoke a `skill` entry from the
session's command list. The Agent MUST treat each reference as the user
explicitly invoking that skill for this prompt, and applies the skill to
the prompt as a whole. The reference carries no input.

An Agent that advertises the `session.prompt.skill` capability accepts one
skill reference per prompt, as the first content block. An Agent that also
advertises `session.prompt.skill.inline` accepts any number of them, at any
position. Clients MUST NOT send a skill reference that the Agent's
capability does not allow.

The `type` discriminator value is `skill`.

One or more `diff --git` sections in Git's `--patch` (`-p`) text format.

Unlike Git, which writes paths relative to the repository root, every
path MUST be absolute, including in `rename from`, `rename to`,
`copy from`, and `copy to` lines, and MUST NOT have a prefix such as
Git's default `a/` and `b/`. Otherwise paths follow Git: `/dev/null`
names the missing side of an added or deleted file in the `---` and
`+++` lines, and paths with unusual characters are quoted as Git quotes
them. Each path, once unquoted, is the same native absolute path string as
the matching `changes` entry. Surrounding commit metadata and email envelopes MUST NOT be
included.

Diff.description:

`patch` optionally carries renderable text for some or all of those changes
and MUST be consistent with `changes`. Agents SHOULD provide `patch` whenever
feasible. Clients MUST handle diffs where `patch` is omitted or `null`.

See protocol docs: [Content](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/tool-calls#content)

Agents SHOULD provide patch text whenever feasible. Omitted and `null` are
equivalent and mean no renderable patch text was provided.

The Agent sends this to the Client to request information from the user,
either via a form or by directing them to a URL.

A session-scoped request follows the aggregate foreground-state contract:
Agents SHOULD report `requires_action` when the whole foreground workflow is
blocked on user action. Once reported, they MUST report `running` when progress
resumes, or `idle` if work ends without resuming. Independent background requests
and request-scoped elicitations do not themselves change session state.

MessageMcpRequest.description:
**UNSTABLE**

Request parameters for `mcp/message`, sent from consumer to provider.

`sessionId` and `toolCallId` name the session and tool call the request was
sent for. Both are optional. The provider can use `sessionId` to choose
which session the request runs for, and `toolCallId` to show the request
with the tool call that the Agent reports. Neither field grants
permission to run the request.

See RFD: [MCP-over-ACP](https://agentclientprotocol.com/rfds/mcp-over-acp#session-and-tool-call-attribution)

serverId.description: The declared ACP MCP server receiving this request.

params.description: Optional inner MCP params. Null is equivalent to omission.

sessionId.description:
The session whose work caused this request. It is the `sessionId` the
Agent uses on `session/update` for that work. For a child session's work,
that is the child's ID.

Optional. Omitted and `null` are equivalent and mean the Agent supplied
no session. The Agent SHOULD include it when it knows the session, and
MUST NOT send another session's ID when it does not. A provider that
needs the session to run the request MAY reject a request without it.

toolCallId.description:
The tool call in that session that this request is part of. It is the
`toolCallId` the Agent uses to report the call in `session/update`. The
Agent SHOULD report the tool call before it sends the request.

Optional. Omitted and `null` are equivalent and mean the Agent supplied
no tool call. The Agent MUST NOT send it without `sessionId`. More than
one request can name the same tool call.

The _meta property is reserved by ACP to allow Clients and Agents to attach additional
metadata to their interactions. Omitted and `null` are equivalent and mean no metadata.
Implementations MUST NOT assign meaning to keys they do not recognize.
This is ACP metadata, not the inner MCP message's `_meta`.

See protocol docs: [Extensibility](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/extensibility)

StateUpdate.description:
A snapshot of the session's aggregate foreground activity.

Foreground work is the Agent's active response or workflow in the session,
including model processing, tool execution, and waiting for user action needed
to continue that work. It can start with a prompt or be Agent-initiated, for
example to pursue an ongoing goal or follow up on a completed background task.
Either way, the Agent MUST report `running` when foreground work starts,
or `requires_action` if it starts blocked on user action, and `idle` when it
ends. The Agent SHOULD include a stop reason on that idle update.
Agent-initiated work does not require a prompt request or a synthetic user
message.

`running` may precede user-message insertion, for example during a foreground
hook. It is not acknowledgment of insertion, and rejecting a prompt does not
itself end foreground work.

Background activity can continue and emit other `session/update` notifications
while `idle`. Those notifications, including a detached task's progress or
completion, do not by themselves change this state. A permission request only
warrants `requires_action` when foreground work is blocked on user action.

The Agent SHOULD report `requires_action` when the foreground workflow as a
whole cannot progress without user action, including permissions or elicitations.
Once reported, it MUST report `running` when progress resumes, or `idle` when
work ends without resuming.
If other foreground work can progress, the state remains `running`. Resolving
one of several requests does not itself change the state. Agents SHOULD ignore
responses for work that has already ended rather than use them to resume it.

A new session defaults to idle until a state update reports otherwise.
Resume MUST send a current-state snapshot after any replay and before its
response. The snapshot reports foreground state after resuming.
The response alone does not imply idle.
Repeated snapshots are idempotent, not additional work or completions.
A repeated state may carry updated information without another state transition.
The Agent MUST report `idle` when no foreground activity remains. Completing
an individual activity while other foreground work continues does not require
an idle boundary. Local commands use the same lifecycle even without model work.

See protocol docs: [Session States](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/prompt-lifecycle#session-states)

ReplayComplete.description:
Marks the end of the history replay requested by `session/resume`.

The Agent MUST send this exactly once on a session for each `session/resume` request
with a `replayFrom` cursor, after the last replayed update for that session
and before the response, even for an empty replay. After receiving the
request, the Agent MUST hold live updates for the session during replay.
If the session is already active on the connection, a live update the Agent
sent earlier can still arrive after the Client sends the request. The marker
signals the end of the requested replay, not its start. A full replay covers
all the history the Agent retained for that session.

The Agent MUST NOT send it when `replayFrom` is omitted or `null`, or when
it cannot finish the replay. A replay that ends without it and without a
successful response is truncated.

See protocol docs: [Replay Complete](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/session-setup#replay-complete)

SubagentUpdate.description:
Notification that the enclosing parent session created and owns a child session.

Later updates modify the existing association's metadata, not its ownership.

Sent on the immediate parent session. The first update for an unknown
`sessionId` announces the child and MUST be sent
before any live request or notification bearing the child's session ID,
including messages naming it as sender or recipient. Child events are
delivered automatically. No separate child resume or subscription is needed.
Understanding this update, registering child sessions, and applying their
operation restrictions are baseline requirements. No Client capability
is required.

Only `sessionId` is required. Other fields have
patch semantics: omitted fields leave the stored value unchanged, `null`
clears or unsets the value, and concrete values replace it. A concrete
`_meta` object instead patches the stored metadata by top-level key. For
`state`, `null` removes the current state report and leaves activity
unconfirmed. It does not report idle or cancellation. A child whose capabilities are
unset permits no Client-initiated session mutations.

`cwd` and `additionalDirectories` report where the Agent placed the child.
While unset, each inherits the immediate parent's effective value.
The title and description provide the parent's display metadata for the
child. Agents SHOULD mirror known child state changes in the parent's
`state` using the same `StateUpdate` snapshot as the
ordinary `state_update` notification on the child session. This reports
child state, not a separate parent-owned lifecycle. Clients MUST
apply duplicate reports idempotently.
Completing or cancelling work does not end the association: the parent may
message the same child again. Individual messages and their outcomes do not
change this association.

See protocol docs: [Subagents](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/subagents)

Optional and nullable. Omitted means unchanged. `null` removes the
current report and leaves activity unconfirmed (not idle or cancelled).
A concrete `StateUpdate` replaces the entire previous snapshot.

Optional and nullable. Omitted means unchanged. `null` clears the
reported value. While unset, the child inherits its immediate parent's
effective additional directories, independently of `cwd`. A concrete
array replaces the whole list. `[]` reports no additional directories.

anyOf.description:
All possible requests that a Client can send to an Agent.

This enum is used internally for routing RPC requests. You typically won't need
to use this directly.

This enum encompasses all method calls from Client to Agent.

anyOf.title: InitializeRequest
anyOf.description:
Establishes the connection with a Client and negotiates protocol capabilities.

This method is called at the beginning of the connection, before any other request, to:
- Negotiate the protocol version to use
- Exchange capability information between Client and Agent
- Determine available authentication methods

The Client MAY repeat it before its first other request. The latest successful
`initialize` is authoritative.

The Agent responds with its supported protocol version and capabilities.

See protocol docs: [Initialization](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/initialization)

anyOf.title: LoginAuthRequest
anyOf.description:
Authenticates the Client using the specified authentication method.

Agents MUST support this method when their `initialize` response included
a non-empty `authMethods` list. Clients MUST call this method only
with a method whose type defines a protocol-driven login flow, and MUST NOT
call it when `authMethods` was omitted or empty.

Called when the Agent requires authentication before allowing session creation.
The Client provides the authentication method ID that was advertised during initialization.

After successful authentication, the Client can proceed to create sessions with
`session/new` without receiving a `-32000` (Authentication required) error.

See protocol docs: [Authentication](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/authentication)

**UNSTABLE**

Lists providers that can be configured by the Client.

anyOf.title: SetProviderRequest
anyOf.description:
**UNSTABLE**

This capability is not part of the spec yet, and may be removed or changed at any point.

Replaces the configuration for a provider.

anyOf.title: DisableProviderRequest
anyOf.description:
**UNSTABLE**

This capability is not part of the spec yet, and may be removed or changed at any point.

Disables a provider.

anyOf.title: LogoutAuthRequest
anyOf.description:
Logs out of the current authenticated state.

Agents MUST support this method when their `initialize` response included
a non-empty `authMethods` list. Clients MUST NOT call this method
when `authMethods` was omitted or empty.

After a successful logout, authentication-gated requests require the
Client to complete an advertised authentication flow again. There is no
guarantee about the behavior of already running sessions.

anyOf.title: AuthStatusRequest
anyOf.description:
**UNSTABLE**

This capability is not part of the spec yet, and may be removed or changed at any point.

Queries the Agent's current authentication state.

This method is only available if the Agent advertises the `auth.status` capability.
It MUST NOT change any Agent state, and Agents MUST NOT reject it with `-32000` (Authentication required).

anyOf.title: NewSessionRequest
anyOf.description:
Creates a new conversation session with the Agent.

Sessions represent independent conversation contexts with their own history and state.

The Agent:
- Creates a new session context
- Connects to the specified MCP servers
- Returns a unique session ID for future requests

Fails with `-32000` (Authentication required) if the Agent requires authentication.

See protocol docs: [Session Setup](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/session-setup)

anyOf.title: ListSessionsRequest
anyOf.description:
Lists existing sessions known to the Agent.

The Agent returns metadata about sessions, with optional filtering and pagination.

anyOf.title: DeleteSessionRequest
anyOf.description:
Deletes an existing session from `session/list`.

This method is only available if the Agent advertises the `session.delete` capability.

anyOf.title: ForkSessionRequest
anyOf.description:
**UNSTABLE**

This capability is not part of the spec yet, and may be removed or changed at any point.

Forks an existing session to create a new independent session.

This method is only available if the Agent advertises the `session.fork` capability.

The Agent creates a new session with the same conversation context as the
original. The fork can be used for operations like generating summaries without
affecting the original session's history.

As with `session/new`, the forked session is active once the Agent responds,
set up with the request's `cwd`, `additionalDirectories`, and `mcpServers`.
The Client can prompt it without calling `session/resume` first.

anyOf.description:
**UNSTABLE**

anyOf.title: SetSessionTitleRequest
anyOf.description:
**UNSTABLE**

anyOf.title: ResumeSessionRequest
anyOf.description:
Resumes an existing session.

The Agent resumes the session context so that the conversation
can continue. If `replayFrom` is set, the Agent replays
retained conversation history before responding.

anyOf.title: CloseSessionRequest
anyOf.description:
Closes an active session and frees up any resources associated with it.

The Agent MUST cancel any ongoing work as if `session/cancel` was called, stop the
session's background work, and then free the resources associated with the session.

anyOf.title: CancelToolCallRequest
anyOf.description:
Cancels one tool call without cancelling the rest of the session's work.

This method is only available while the tool call advertises `capabilities.cancel`.
The response means the Agent accepted the cancellation. A final `tool_call_update`
confirms it.

anyOf.title: CancelTerminalRequest
anyOf.description:
Stops one terminal's process without cancelling the rest of the session's work.

This method is only available while the terminal advertises `capabilities.cancel`.
The response means the Agent accepted the cancellation. A `terminal_update` with
`exitStatus` confirms it.

anyOf.title: SetSessionConfigOptionRequest
anyOf.description: Sets the current value for a session configuration option.

anyOf.title: PromptRequest
anyOf.description:
Processes a user prompt within a session.

Acceptance means adding a logical user message with an ID and a position
relative to other messages in the ACP conversation, not receipt or queueing.
The Agent MUST return the inserted message's ID without waiting for
processing to finish.

The Agent reports the user message with the same ID through `session/update`.
This notification can arrive before or after the response, and MUST NOT
precede insertion. Processing state, output, tool calls, and completion are
also reported through session updates.

An error response means the user message was not inserted. Once it is
inserted, the Agent MUST NOT answer with an error, even if the work fails
before the response is sent. It ends that work with the `error` stop reason.

A rejected submission produces no user-message updates. Foreground state
follows its normal lifecycle independently of the request outcome:
`running` may precede insertion, and rejection alone does not imply `idle`.

See protocol docs: [Prompt Lifecycle](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/prompt-lifecycle)

anyOf.title: ExtMethodRequest

Extension methods are custom methods that are not part of the ACP spec.

See protocol docs: [Extensibility](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/extensibility)

Request parameters for closing an active session.

The Agent MUST cancel any ongoing work related to the session as if `session/cancel`
was called, then free the resources associated with the session. Unlike `session/cancel`,
closing also stops the session's background work. After the close response, the Agent
sends no notifications or requests for the session on that connection. It still
answers `session/prompt` requests that were pending.

treat a `-32002` response as a successful close.

When closing cancels active foreground work, the Agent MUST send the final
updates for that work and the idle `state_update` with `stopReason: "cancelled"`
before responding successfully to `session/close`. Closing an idle session
does not itself require another idle update.

Closing also cancels pending `session/prompt` requests whose messages have not
been inserted, including held prompts. If closing prevents a prompt's user message from being inserted, the
Agent MUST answer that request with `-32800` (Request cancelled). If the message
has already been inserted, the Agent MUST respond successfully with its
`messageId`. Prompt responses need not precede the close response.

As a baseline, the Agent MUST support `text` and `resource_link` content blocks,
while other variants are optionally enabled via `PromptCapabilities`.

The Client MUST adapt its interface according to `PromptCapabilities`.

The Client MAY include referenced pieces of context as either
`resource` or `resource_link` content blocks.

When available, `resource` is preferred
as it avoids extra round-trips and allows the message to include
pieces of context from sources the Agent might not have access to.

inserting it.

submission. Agents that advertise `capabilities.session` MUST support the key.
A retry of a recorded insertion returns the original `messageId` without inserting
another message.

The Agent MUST recognize the key for as long as it retains the message, including

This enum is used internally for routing RPC notifications. You typically won't need

anyOf.title: CancelSessionNotification
anyOf.description:
Cancels the named session's active foreground work and earlier prompts not yet inserted.
The Agent MUST answer those uninserted prompts with `-32800`. Inserted prompts still
succeed with their `messageId`. This cancellation does not cover later submissions.

Work in the latest `background` list is not covered and keeps running. The
Agent MAY stop background activity it does not list.

Upon receiving this notification, the Agent SHOULD stop all language model
requests and all tool call invocations of the cancelled foreground work as soon
as possible.

The Agent MUST stop waiting for pending `session/request_permission` requests of
the cancelled work and treat them as not approved. It MUST cancel each of them
with `$/cancel_request`.

When cancellation stops active foreground work, the Agent MUST send that work's
pending updates, then an idle `state_update` with `stopReason: "cancelled"`,
before starting new foreground work in the same session. A later prompt can be
inserted and acknowledged before that idle update, or held with its response
pending. Listed background work can report updates before or after it.
No additional idle update is required if no foreground work was active.

After cancellation completes, the Agent SHOULD ignore late answers rather
than use them to resume the cancelled work.

Agents MUST catch errors caused by aborting cancelled work and report the
`cancelled` stop reason, not `error`.

See protocol docs: [Cancellation](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/draft/prompt-lifecycle#cancellation)

A conductor sends `proxy/initialize` instead of `initialize` to every component that has a
successor, which tells the component to run as a proxy. The params and the response are
